notes: All evals assume the subagent runs with cwd set to a real repo checkout. where-to-start is a router: it runs the artifact-scan routine, then names WHERE in the product lifecycle to enter and WHICH skill to run next. It is read-only — it never writes artifacts. The 'files' array seeds lifecycle artifacts to fix which stages are satisfied so the recommended entry point is deterministic.

evals.name: trigger-match
evals.prompt: i've got this repo and honestly no idea where to start — which skill should i even use?
evals.expected_output: The where-to-start skill is selected (not ideate, artifact-scan, or a downstream producer skill directly). The agent runs the artifact scan and reports a single recommended entry point.

assertions.text: The where-to-start skill is the one selected for this prompt
The agent runs the artifact-scan routine rather than duplicating the scan logic inline
The response names exactly one recommended next skill to run

evals.name: empty-repo-enters-at-ideate
evals.prompt: where do i start with this project?
evals.expected_output: With no lifecycle artifacts present, every stage is unsatisfied, so the earliest gap is ideate. The router recommends entering at the ideate stage and running the ideate skill.

assertions.text: The response reports all six lifecycle stages (ideate, approach, roadmap, PRD, plan, tickets) with satisfied/not-satisfied/unknown markers
The response identifies ideate as the earliest unsatisfied stage / entry point
The response recommends running the ideate skill
The agent does not create or edit any lifecycle artifact (read-only)

evals.name: approach-present-enters-at-roadmap
evals.prompt: we've already aligned on an approach doc — what should i run next?
evals.expected_output: With an ideate report and ./docs/approach.md present but no roadmap, the earliest gap is roadmap. The router recommends entering at the roadmap stage and running to-roadmap.

files.content:
# Ideate report

Seed idea report so the ideate stage is satisfied.

# Approach

What we are building and why — alignment captured.

assertions.text: The response marks ideate and approach as satisfied, citing the seeded files as evidence
The response identifies roadmap as the earliest unsatisfied stage / entry point
The response recommends running to-roadmap — the roadmap-producing skill
The response does not recommend re-running ideate or chat-to-approach for already-satisfied stages
The agent does not create or edit any lifecycle artifact (read-only)
